pr_title: Add nullptr checks to efi DeviceHandle and FilePath
pr_comments:
codewise looks good, but please add comments, that explain these checks, as suggested.

also, please explain in the commit msg what is going on here.

commit msg title should start with `stub: `  or so.

commit msg should include text `Fixes: #29331`

looks good, but the commit msg is a bit misleading. If grub wanted it could support the FilePath/DeviceHandle protocols just fine, it just does not. Hence it has nothing to do with "when using a bootloader to load the image from a partition with a file system that is not supported by the firmware" as the commit msg says, but is simply a limitation of Grub.

Hence please update the commit msg to say something like "when using a boot loader that does not implement the FilePath/DeviceHandle fields of the invoked EFI_LOADED_IMAGE protocol, such as Grub"

issue_context.title: Systemd-stub fails to boot if booted by grub on non-efi readable partition
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

254.4-2

### Used distribution

Arch

### Linux kernel version used

6.5.4-arch2-1

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-stub

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

I have a UKI generated by ukify, sitting on an ext4 formatted boot partition. As this partition is not readable by my uefi, i would expect systemd-stub to not check for additional files and just boot Linux.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

 When my UKI is called by grub, grub passes `null` as the `DeviceHandle` in the loaded image protocol. `systemd-stub` asserts the device handle to be non-null, causing the boot to fail, and shows the very non-helpful error message
```
systemd-boot: Assertion 'device' failed at ../systemd-stable/src/boot/efi/part-discovery.c:251@partition_open, halting.
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Use the grub `chainloader` command to boot a UKI containing `systemd-stub`, which is loaded from an ext4 partition.

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments:
I could make a PR replacing the assert in [`partition_open`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/5808300c442359aea1ad4c0d1eb3e7717673bd38/src/boot/efi/part-discovery.c#L251) with a check, and returning an error, if it `device` is null. As errors are already ignored in [`run`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/5808300c442359aea1ad4c0d1eb3e7717673bd38/src/boot/efi/stub.c#L397), this would just cause `systemd-stub` to boot normally.

I don't know, how to test that though, `ukify` doesn't allow me, to specify a custom stub.

> I don't know, how to test that though, `ukify` doesn't allow me, to specify a custom stub.

It always had the `--stub` option exactly for that.
